metadata.title: Function Composition: Two Orders
metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.objective: Show g(x) then f(g(x)) as a two-stage machine or graph mapping.
expectedUnderstanding: The intermediate value is g(x) or f(x)
The final value is f(g(x)) or g(f(x))
Changing the order changes the result for these functions

checkpoints.title: Trace both lanes
checkpoints.body: Set x to 0. The top intermediate is g(0) = 2 and the top final is f(2) = 3. The bottom intermediate is f(0) = -1 and the bottom final is g(-1) = 1.5.

checkpoints.title: Same input, different output
checkpoints.body: Set x to 1. Top: g(1) = 2.5, then f(2.5) = 4. Bottom: f(1) = 1, then g(1) = 2.5. The two final markers are at different heights.

checkpoints.title: Order matters here
checkpoints.body: Set x to 1.5. Top final f(g(1.5)) = 4.5; bottom final g(f(1.5)) = 3. Composition is substitution, not multiplication, and these orders do not commute.

narration.text: One input feeds two lanes. The top applies g then f; the bottom applies f then g.
The middle marker is the intermediate value; the right marker is the composed output.
The two final markers separate, so swapping the order changes the result for these functions.

fallback.text: An input x feeds two orders: top applies g then f, bottom applies f then g. The middle dot is g(x) or f(x); the right marker is the composed output. With g(x)=0.5x+2 and f(u)=2u-1, the orders give x+3 and x+1.5, so they differ.

accessibility.alt: Two composition lanes from one input: the top applies g then f, the bottom f then g. Circles mark the top lane and squares the bottom; a slider changes x, and the final markers sit at different heights.
